title: Pulmonary embolism (India)
specialty: Emergency Medicine / Pulmonology / Cardiology / Internal Medicine

evidenceAudit.scope: Acute pulmonary embolism (PE) in adults in India: pre-test probability, D-dimer and computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA), risk stratification, anticoagulation, thrombolysis for high-risk PE, early discharge, pregnancy and duration, using the ESC 2019 PE guideline (ACC summary), NICE NG158 and US labels, because no Indian national PE guideline was found.
findings: High-risk definitions (cardiac arrest, obstructive shock, systolic BP below 90 mmHg or a fall of 40 mmHg or more for over 15 minutes), PESI and sPESI tiers, RV dysfunction markers, PERC, age-adjusted D-dimer, DOAC regimens, VKA target INR 2.0–3.0, thrombolysis for high-risk PE, Hestia early discharge, pregnancy and duration checked against the ACC summary of ESC 2019.

Two-level PE Wells score (above 4 likely), CTPA, V/Q alternatives, outpatient care and unstable PE (UFH plus thrombolysis; no thrombolysis in stable PE) checked against NICE NG158; alteplase 100 mg over 2 hours from its US label.
unverifiedSections: No Indian national PE guideline was found.
ESC 2019 is used through the ACC summary, not the full guideline text.
Tenecteplase and reduced-dose thrombolysis are not dosed here.
Paediatric PE is outside the scope of the cited sources (apixaban paediatric dosing is in the DVT topic).
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Pulmonary embolism is obstruction of the pulmonary arteries by thrombus, usually from leg or pelvic veins. Sudden rise in pulmonary vascular resistance strains the right ventricle; if it fails, cardiac output falls and shock follows. Risk ranges from small peripheral emboli to high-risk PE with haemodynamic instability, which carries high early mortality. Diagnosis follows a pre-test probability score, D-dimer when probability is low, and CTPA. Haemodynamically unstable patients need systemic thrombolysis; others are anticoagulated, preferably with a DOAC, for at least 3 months (ESC 2019; NICE NG158).
keyMechanisms: Thrombus from deep veins lodges in pulmonary arteries.
Raised pulmonary vascular resistance dilates and strains the right ventricle.
RV failure lowers LV filling and cardiac output, causing shock.

physicalSigns: Hypotension, raised JVP in high-risk PE
redFlags: Systolic BP below 90 mmHg or vasopressors needed (ESC 2019)
Fall in systolic BP of 40 mmHg or more for over 15 minutes (ESC 2019)
RV dysfunction with raised troponin (intermediate-high risk)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Electrocardiogram (ECG) ischaemia and troponin pattern; normal CTPA.
Pulmonary oedema, raised BNP, LV dysfunction.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Cardiac arrest, obstructive shock, or persistent hypotension.
Elevated PESI with both RV dysfunction and raised troponin.
RV/LV ratio 1.0 or more on echo or computed tomography (CT); TAPSE below 16 mm.

clinicalManagement.title: Haemodynamically unstable (high risk)
actions: Unfractionated heparin (UFH) infusion and systemic thrombolysis (NICE NG158; ESC 2019 Class I).
Thrombolysis fails or contraindicated: surgical embolectomy or catheter-directed treatment (ESC 2019).
Do not thrombolyse haemodynamically stable PE (NICE NG158).

clinicalManagement.title: Stable PE
actions: Start anticoagulation while awaiting imaging if probability is high or intermediate (ESC 2019).
Stratify with PESI or sPESI, RV imaging and troponin (ESC 2019).
Intermediate-high: anticoagulate and monitor closely for rescue reperfusion.

clinicalManagement.title: Anticoagulant choice
actions: DOAC preferred (ESC 2019 Class I; NICE NG158 apixaban or rivaroxaban).
DOACs contraindicated in severe renal impairment, pregnancy, lactation and antiphospholipid syndrome (ESC 2019).

clinicalManagement.title: Early discharge
actions: Low-risk PE with negative Hestia criteria and follow-up in place can be treated as outpatients (ESC 2019; NICE NG158).

clinicalManagement.title: Duration and follow-up
actions: At least 3 months; stop at 3 months if major transient risk factor (ESC 2019).
Recurrent VTE without transient factor or antiphospholipid syndrome: indefinite (ESC 2019).
Review at 3–6 months; echo or V/Q scan for persistent breathlessness (CTEPH screen) (ESC 2019).

medicationPlan.note: Regimens from the ESC 2019 summary, NICE NG158 and US labels (apixaban, dabigatran, enoxaparin, alteplase). No Indian national PE guideline was found. India-only topic; the Saudi topic is unchanged. Not clinically reviewed.

teaching.scope: Acute PE in Indian emergency practice.
learningObjectives: Use Wells, D-dimer and CTPA correctly.
Stratify risk and identify high-risk PE.
keyPoints: Unstable PE: UFH plus alteplase 100 mg over 2 hours.
Stable PE: DOAC first; LMWH in pregnancy.
At least 3 months; review at 3–6 months.
pitfalls: Delaying anticoagulation while waiting for CTPA.
DOAC in pregnancy or antiphospholipid syndrome.
